description_en: The three-storey Bhairava temple is based on a square plan measuring 257 cm on each side, and is based on a stone plinth that is 30 cm high and measures a length of 365 cm on each side. The temple has openings on all four sides, the main entrance is at the south. It is clad with repousse brass sheets and guarded by stone lions on either side. Each opening has an archedtoraṇaresting on a pair of colonnettes, which in turn sit on stone blocks. The latticework at the opening to the north is still intact, while the latticework on the east and west openings has been lost and replaced by metal grill works.This south-facing temple has three brass roofs. The second and third tier are supported by 12 struts each, while the ground floor has four corner timber posts supporting the multi-layer carved timber cornice bands, above which timber windows have been carved on all four sides. These are sheltered under the large overhang of the first tier roof, which is clad in brass sheets. This roof tier is supported by 20 struts (out of which 4 are corner struts and the remaining 16 have iconic carvings). Four small flags hang down from the fringes of the top roof. Above the pinnacle is a metal parasol. According to an inscription mentioned in an unpublished record by Heimo Rau, the temple was built in 1727 CE. Lettering in Devanāgarī script has been inscribed on the fringes of two upper floors, and informs readers of the name of the temple (Koṭarākṣa Bhairava) and of its renovation in (1904 CE (NS 1024). On top of the first roof in the sanctum is a stone image of Bhairava.The struts:East, 1st floor: Bhairava, Maheśvarī, Bhairava, Brahmayāṇī; 2nd floor: Brahmayāṇī, Indrayāṇī; 3rd floor: Bhairava, BhairavaSouth, 1st floor: Bhairava, Vaiṣṇavī, Bhairava, Kaumārī; 2nd floor: Varāhī, Vaiṣṇavī; 3rd floor: Bhairava, BhairavaWest, 1st floor: Bhairava, Indrayāṇī, Bhairava, Varrāhī; 2nd floor: Kaumārī, Cāmuṇḍā; 3rd floor: Bhairava, BhairavaNorth, 1st floor: Bhairava, Bhagavatī, Bhairava, Cāmuṇḍa; 2nd floor: Bhagavatī, Maheśvarī; 3rd floor: Bhairava, BhairavaOn thetoraṇaabove the main door, one can find a Bhairava statue (constructed in brass in NS 1033) flanked by Gaṇeśa and Kumāra inālīḍhaandpratyālīḍhapostures on either side. There are carved wooden windows facing in all four directions on the two upper floors, and in three directions on the first floor. Images of various deities have been carved on the struts (ṭũḍālas). Statues of two sitting lions have been placed on both sides of the main entrance, and behind the two lion statues are two brass banners. A bell is hanging to the left of the main entrance, upon which the date of its donation (NS 1033 /1913 CE) is inscribed. Eight auspicious signs (aṣṭamaṅgalas) have been carved on the stone beam that supports the bell. There are images of mice on both sides of the beam and an image of Jvālānhāyakaṃ in the middle. A Kavã and Khyāḥ have recently been added to the walls to the main entrance on the left- and right-hand side respectively. Oil lamps, heightened and supported by a wooden structure, surround the temple in a row. On the western plinth of the temple is an image of Umāmaheśvara. Next to this image are two inscriptions. Aliṅgahas been established on the northern side of the temple.The main sanctum is below ground level, almost 110 cm below the main entry level, and can be accessed via stone steps. A metal stair with a handrail was added recently. The main deity is in its non-iconic form, and sits in a niche framed by a metal repousse. The east wall has a niche with a hole exactly above the shrine (dyaḥpvaḥ), allowing the unhindered circulation of unspecified spirits. The sanctum has stone flooring; the space in front of the main entrance (approx. 470 cm x 235 cm) is stone-paved. There is a stone slab showing a carved human body (in a prostrate form, ormhadanā vanegu) and a circular lotus leaf (padmapatra) in line with the main entrance. All the floors have carved windows on each side.Exactly behind the temple, to the north, is a square sunken pit with a width of 70cm on each side, and a depth of 30cm. This has aliṅga. Almost half of the pit is below the plinth level.
description_ne: इखालखु टोलमा रहेको यो मन्दिर दक्षिणतर्फ फर्किएको छ र मन्दिरका तीनै वटा छाना पित्तलले छाइएका छन् । तेस्रो छानामाथि गजुर छ र त्यसमाथि छत्र राखिएको छ । मन्दिरको सबैभन्दा माथिल्लो छानाको चार कुनामा झल्लरमुनि चतुर्महाराज झुण्ड्याइएका छन् । मथिल्ला दुई छानाका झल्लरमा देवनागरी लिपिमा मन्दिको नाम कोटराक्ष भैरव र यसको पुनर्निर्माण ने. सं. १०२४ मा भएको भन्ने जानकारी दिइएको छ । पहिलो छानाको फेदमा एउटा पीठिका राखिएको छ जसमा भैरवको मूर्ति राखिएको छ । भैरवको दायाँ र बायाँ उनका सहचर रहेका छन् भने माथि तोरण रहेको छ । मन्दिरको मूल ढोकामाथिको पित्तलको तोरण ने. सं. १०३३ मा बनेको हो जसमा बीचमा भैरवको मूर्ति र दायाँ र बायाँ गणेश र कुमारका मूर्ति आलीढ र प्रत्यालीढ मुद्रामा रहेका छन् । माथिल्ला दुई तलाका चारै दिशामा र  तल्लो तलाको तीन दिशामा रहेका  काठका झ्यालहरू राम्ररी कुँदिएका छन् । टुँडालहरूमा विभिन्न देवीदेवताका मूर्तिहरू कुँदिएका छन् । मन्दिरको प्रवेशद्वारको दुई छेउमा बसेका दुई वटा सिंहका प्रतिमा छन् र तिनीहरूको पछाडि पित्तलका दुईवटा पताका राखिएका छन् ।  प्रवेशद्वारको बायाँपट्टि एउटा घण्ट राखिएको छ जसमा उक्त  घण्ट चढाइएको मिति ने. सं. १०३३ अङ्कित छ ।  घण्ट झुण्ड्याइएको ढुङ्गामा अष्टमङ्गल कुँदिएको छ । त्यस ढुङ्गामा दुई छेउमा मुसाको प्रतिमा र बीचमा ज्वालान्हायकं राखिएको छ ।  प्रवेशद्वारको बायाँपट्टि भित्तामा कवँ र  दायाँपट्टि ख्याको हालसालै कोरिएको चित्र छ । मन्दिरको वरिपरि दीपावलि राखिएको छ । मन्दिरको पश्चिमपट्टि पेटीमा  उमामहेश्वरको मूर्ति छ।त्यसको नजिकै दुईवटा शिलालेख राखिएका छन् । मन्दिरको उत्तरपट्टि एउटा लिङ्ग प्रतिष्ठापन गरिएको छ ।
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths)

historical_events.event_description: A stone inscription with a hymn (śloka) dedicated to Bhairava is located inside the temple. It is attached to the wall above the main deity.
Golden vessel and flags were offered to the god by Daivajñamanyarāja Bhāro (the son of Siddhirāja Bhāro).
Reconstruction of Ṭīkābhairava temple and offering ofsalipauto Śvetabhairava Koṭarākṣanātha by Kājī Ratna Bahādura Jośī and his wife Ramā Kumārī Jośī.
